The Belief Simplex

How a transformer trained by reward alone comes to hold its hidden-goal posterior as probabilities, seen on the triangle the posterior lives on.

Six 2-block transformers (width 128), PPO on reward only in a hidden-goal bandit with an exact belief-MDP solver; twelve more for the channel follow-up. Pre-registered plans, then measurement; the simplex figures and the quadratic maps are post-hoc additions. Repository paths: studies/2_belief_state/reward_bandit, studies/2_belief_state/belief_formation, studies/2_belief_state/channel_bandit.

  1. Counting is free. An untrained attention over the history already gives the token counts (R² 0.98); training makes the pattern less even, not more.
  2. Block 0's MLP makes the probability code. Extrapolation of the probabilities goes from 0.33 at its input to 0.75 at its output; the untrained MLP gives 0.10. Block 1's attention carries that code from earlier positions and block 1's MLP finishes it (0.85).
  3. On the simplex, the MLP is a fold. A probe fitted on uncertain states sends the untrained network's confident states out of the triangle along straight lines; block 0's MLP bends them back toward the vertices and the final state puts them on the corners.
  4. A softmax decoder cannot see the fold. Decoding logits through a softmax keeps every belief inside the triangle and recovers the posterior from the untrained network as well as from the trained one (0.85 against 0.82), because the decoder supplies the nonlinearity itself; the affine probe is what tells the two codes apart.
  5. The fold is a count lookup, half quadratic. A quadratic in the log-odds substituted for the MLPs recovers half of what an affine map loses (0.158 to 0.108). Trained on cues whose order matters, block 0 still computes nothing order-dependent (0.04 of the belief difference between two orders at its MLP output); block 1's attention makes the order-dependent belief (0.53) and the policy follows it (it changes its first action where it should in 0.56 of pairs, control 0.11).
  6. The policy pays for the fold. A decision affine in the exact log-odds costs 0.158 of regret; affine in the exact probabilities, 0.062. Within a step the final state is a nearly flat image of the simplex (0.91 affine in the probabilities, two components hold 0.96 of its variance), striped by the count lattice.

The task and what "probability space" means here

A goal among three is hidden. The agent sees four noisy cue tokens, then makes six decisions among four actions whose Bernoulli reward probabilities depend on the goal, and it sees each reward, so rewards are evidence too. Every likelihood is a product over independent draws, so the posterior depends on the history only through its counts, the belief MDP has 210 210 states, and Q* is exact.

Two parametrisations of the same belief matter. The log-odds y are affine in the counts, so any network that sums token embeddings holds them. The probabilities b = softmax(y) are what the Bayes value is linear in. The reward-bandit experiment found the transformer's final state extrapolates b (0.85) where an untrained network and a GRU extrapolate only y. This page is about where that comes from.

The belief of a decision state is a point of a triangle with vertices G1, G2, G3. In every figure below a point is coloured by its exact belief as RGB = (p1, p2, p3), so a state certain of G1 is red, one certain of G3 is blue, and uncertain states are muddy.

Three things to read off. The counts are there before training and attention does not improve on them. The log-odds never extrapolate beyond 0.50 from any trained site although the counts they are affine in are held at 0.9. And the probability code appears across one component: block 0's MLP, whose input extrapolates b at 0.33 and whose output at 0.75.

The fold, seen on the triangle

The discriminating picture. The probe is fitted on the uncertain states only (grey: their exact beliefs, every log-odds below 2 nats) and applied to the confident ones, whose decoded beliefs are drawn in colour.

In distribution this picture is unavailable: an affine probe fitted on all states fills a recognisable triangle at every site, trained or not (R² 0.93 to 0.99), which is the in-distribution non-result the belief-state study has reported before.

A softmax decoder

An affine probe can place a decoded belief outside the triangle, which is what made the figure above diagnostic. The alternative is to decode logits and pass them through a softmax, z = Wx + c, p̂ = softmax(z), fitted by cross-entropy to the exact posterior. Then every decoded belief is non-negative and sums to one, so it lies inside the simplex by construction. Fitted on the same uncertain states and applied to the confident ones:

EXT R² of baffine probesoftmax decodersoftmax decoder, in distribution
trained mid00.330.580.96
trained mlp00.750.810.98
trained res20.850.820.98
untrained res20.090.850.97
untrained mid0−1.130.880.97

The two probes answer different questions. The softmax decoder asks whether the posterior is recoverable at all, and it is, from either network, because the decoder supplies the fold itself; it therefore cannot tell a log-odds code from a probability code. The affine probe asks which parametrisation the state is linear in, and its extrapolation failure on the untrained network is exactly the fold that block 0's MLP later makes. Median over six seeds: untrained final state 0.85 through the softmax against 0.09 through the affine probe; trained 0.82 against 0.85.

What the components compute

IID R² of each component's output at decision positions from functions of the belief. A table over belief states is any function of the belief; it generalises (cross-validated 0.996 on the final state, from 3 247 distinct states visited about 30 times each).

componentaffine in yaffine in bquadratic in ythe step alonebelief-node table

attn10.620.720.670.110.994

Every component's output is a function of the belief state, and none is affine in either parametrisation. The code is probability-like: a nonlinear function of the log-odds that extrapolates in b rather than y, not the probabilities themselves.

Does the policy need the fold?

The policy re-run in the environment with a component's output at the decision token replaced by its mean at that step, or by its best affine fit from the exact log-odds or the exact probabilities of the current state. The registered patch left block 1's attention free to import the probability code that block 0's MLP had made at earlier positions, so the last three rows, added after a one-seed smoke run, cut that route as well.

patch at the decision tokenexact regretEXT R² b at the final state
none0.0460.85
mlp0 replaced by its mean0.2010.72
mlp1 replaced by its mean0.0520.79
attn0 replaced by its mean0.7360.32
both MLPs affine in the exact log-odds0.080−0.22
both MLPs affine in the exact probabilities0.0271.00
attn1 mean + both MLPs affine in the log-odds (post hoc)0.158−0.20
attn1 mean + both MLPs affine in the probabilities (post hoc)0.0621.00

With the import route cut, a decision affine in the exact log-odds costs 0.158 of regret against 0.062 for the same network affine in the exact probabilities. The nonlinearity is worth about 0.1 of regret, more than the model's distance from the myopic policy (0.068). Replacing the MLPs by affine functions of the exact probabilities improves on the network's own 0.046, so the affine-in-probability part of what the MLPs compute is all the heads use.

How curved the embedding is

Fits of the activations from functions of the belief within each step, pooled over steps; the step itself is a large part of the variance and the node includes it. Median over six seeds.

siteaffine in yaffine in bcubic in bMLP from (b, step)node tablePCA within a step: top 2 / 3

untrained res20.670.680.740.700.9580.58 / 0.72

So the manifold is a curved embedding of the simplex, but only mildly curved: nearly flat within a step, folded at the corners, with the discrete count structure on it. The untrained network's is a plane of log-odds.

Two follow-ups

The MLP as a low-order function of the log-odds

Block 0's MLP output fitted from the exact log-odds y with second- or third-order terms, then substituted for the MLP at the decision token, with block 1's attention cut so the code cannot be imported from earlier positions.

both MLPs replaced by, with attn1 cutexact regret
affine in the log-odds0.158
quadratic in the log-odds0.108
cubic in the log-odds0.094
affine in the probabilities0.062
none (natural; the quadratic with attn1 in place: 0.044)0.046

A quadratic in the log-odds recovers half of what the affine map loses, a cubic a little more, and with block 1's attention left in place the quadratic alone keeps the natural regret. The in-distribution fit of block 0's MLP output rises from 0.41 affine to 0.53 quadratic and 0.63 cubic in the log-odds, against 0.56 affine in the probabilities. To that extent, the probability geometry block 0's MLP makes is a quadratic in the log-odds, with the rest higher order.

Matched-evidence counterfactuals: is the MLP a count lookup?

Under i.i.d. cues the counts fix the posterior, so a network acting on the belief cannot be told from one applying a static count-to-probability lookup. Six new transformers were trained on 8 cues passed through the sticky reliability channel of the hidden goal study, with persistence 0.8 and a hit rate of 0.7 when on, so that the same counts in a different order give a different exact posterior; six more were trained on i.i.d. cues as the control. Both arms were measured on the same channel-generated cues. Each episode's cues and a random permutation of them form a matched pair; Δb is the belief difference between the two orders (median 0.08, a quarter of pairs at or above 0.2; the optimal first action differs in 7.5 percent).

matched pairs, first decisionchannel armi.i.d. controluntrained
exact regret of the policy0.0120.0592.59
where the optimal action differs between the orders: the greedy action differs0.560.110.05
there: right on both orders0.480.040.00
R² of Δb from the belief decoded at block 0's MLP output0.040.000.01
… at block 1's attention output0.53 (0.70 where Δb ≥ 0.2)0.030.06
… at the final state0.58 (0.74)0.010.03

The channel-trained policy separates the two orders in the Bayes direction: where they call for different first actions it changes its action in 0.56 of pairs and is right on both in 0.48, against 0.11 and 0.04 for the control. But nothing in block 0 does: the belief difference decoded at block 0's MLP output explains 0.04 of the exact difference, the same as in the order-blind control. Block 0's MLP is a count-to-probability lookup. The order-dependent belief is made by block 1's attention, which reads the block-0 states of the earlier positions, each holding its own prefix's count-based belief, and it is what the heads read. That is the same route by which, in the i.i.d. task, block 1 imported the probability code from earlier positions.

Registered rule: the channel arm learned; the behavioural criterion missed its control bound by 0.01 (the i.i.d. models change 11 percent of actions where 10 was allowed); the representational criterion failed at block 0's MLP and held at the final state. One of five expectations held, two in part; the expectation that the order-dependent belief would first appear in block 0 was wrong.

Scorecard

  • FORM (the first site whose EXT R² of b reaches 0.6 is an MLP output or the residual after one): held, at mlp0.
  • GATHER (block 0's attention holds the counts at 0.9 or more and the embedding at 0.3 or less): failed by the letter, 0.88 and 0.53. The embedding of the decision token already carries the step and the last event.
  • NONLIN (both MLPs affine in the log-odds raises regret to 0.15 or more): failed as registered, 0.080, because block 1's attention imported the code; held with that route cut, 0.158.
  • Four of seven expectations held, one in part.

Limits

Patches act at the decision position only; the post-hoc combinations cut block 1's attention instead of patching the earlier positions. Affine fits use the exact belief, which hands the patched network cleaner information than it had. The cues are i.i.d., so counts are sufficient and the cue phase cannot separate a filter from a tally. One task; six models; the simplex analysis is post hoc and the extrapolation figures show seed 0.
